headline: Approved 3-2 revisions to Policy Students 501 on transgender student athletics, plus student tuition and activities policies and the 2026/2027 Middle School Handbook.
summary: The committee approved revisions to three student policies, covering non-resident tuition, participation in public school activities, and transgender student athletics. It also approved job descriptions for a 21st Century Program Coordinator, a School Safety Facilitator, and a Career Pathway and Work-Based Learning Coordinator.
decisions: Approved the June 17, 2026 Policy Committee meeting minutes.

Agreed to restore the Assembly and Petition section to the Middle School Handbook.
Approved, as amended, the 2026/2027 Middle School Handbook and forwarded it to the full Board, all in favor.

plain_text:
MANCHESTER SCHOOL DISTRICT SAU #37 
POLICY COMMITTEE  
 
August 19, 2026 6:00 p.m. Or Immediately following  
 
1. Chair Want called the meeting to order at 5:42 p.m. 
 
2. The Clerk calls the roll.  
 
  Present: Committee Members Want, O’Neil, Potter, Taylor, and St. John. 
 
   
3. Public Forum 
 
There was no one present to give public comment. 
 
 
6. Approval of the Minutes from the June 17, 2026 Policy Committee meeting. 
 
On motion of Committee Member Taylor, duly seconded by Committee Member O’Neil-Wong, it was 
moved to approve the minutes of the June 17, 2026 Policy Committee.  All were in favor and the motion 
passed. 
 
 
7. Presentations 
 
There were no presentations this evening. 
 
At this time, the committee took item #15 out of order. 
 
15. 21st Century Program Coordinator – by Alex Levesque, 21st Century Program    
Director 
 
Alex Levesque, Program Director for the 21st Century Program, presented proposed revisions to the 
Program Coordinator job description.  Mr. Levesque explained that the position is a full-time role 
funded specifically through the 21st Century Program and is not covered by a collective bargaining 
agreement.  The position had become vacant for the first time since 2018, providing an opportunity to 
review and update the salary, duties, and responsibilities.
August 19, 2026 Policy Committee  
Page 2 of 13 
 
The Program Coordinator is responsible for daily programming that engages and supports students 
participating in the 21st Century Program.  The proposed revisions were intended to: 
 establish a competitive but sustainable salary; 
 update duties and responsibilities; 
 provide advancement opportunities for current 21st Century staff; and 
 distinguish the position from other coordinator positions within the program. 
 
Questions and comments of the committee included: 
1. Committee Member Potter noted that the revised position appeared to include responsibility for 
coordinating a program site as well as new supervisory duties.  Mr. Levesque explained that 
current site coordinators generally work approximately 30 hours per week. The revised position 
was intentionally structured so that a current site coordinator could potentially advance into the 
new role and increase to a 40-hour schedule. 
2. The revised job description also included oversight and supervision of program staff, volunteers, 
stipend positions, and part-time hourly employees.  Committee Member Potter expressed 
concern that the position had become broader and more demanding while remaining relatively 
modestly compensated.  Chair Want agreed and asked whether the grant could support a larger 
salary.  Mr. Levesque explained that the proposed salary was developed in consideration of other 
positions in the program. 
3. An academic coordinator position had previously been budgeted at approximately $50,000, 
although the District was not currently recruiting for that position.  The Program Coordinator 
would not require teacher certification or similar credentials, the proposed salary was set at 
approximately $45,000. 
4. Mr. Levesque stated that the prior version of the position had carried a significant workload and 
had resulted in burnout. Some District-level responsibilities were therefore being shifted to him 
while the revised role would remain focused on appropriate program-level duties. 
5. The position is funded through multiple 21st Century grants, of which the program currently has 
approximately 14. 
6. The Committee noted that the proposed salary was relatively comparable to an entry-level 
teaching salary, while the Program Coordinator would not necessarily require the same 
certification requirements.
August 19, 2026 Policy Committee  
Page 3 of 13 
 
7. Mr. Levesque also clarified that the grant must cover salary as well as benefits and associated 
employment costs.  The position is based on a 210-day work year. 
8. Committee Member O’Neil Wong recommended revising the minimum qualifications to read 
that a bachelor’s degree is preferred or comparable/relevant experience may be considered.   Mr. 
Levesque agreed to make that change. 
9. The Committee also requested that multilingual preferred be added to the job description. 
10. Committee Member St. John asked whether there was an established maximum salary that could 
be paid from the grant.  Mr. Levesque stated that there was not a specific salary maximum 
written into the grant itself. The practical limitation is the available grant budget. He indicated 
that approximately $45,000 was a figure he believed could be supported appropriately, although 
approximately $50,000 might potentially be possible depending upon the overall grant budget.  
He explained that the previous incumbent had earned approximately $41,000 after multiple cost-
of-living adjustments, making it necessary to increase the starting salary if the District wanted to 
recruit successfully. 
11. Mr. Levesque also confirmed that 21st Century positions generally receive cost-of-living 
increases approved through the annual budget process. 
 
On motion of Committee Member Potter, duly seconded by Committee Member O’Neil-Wong, it was 
moved to approve the revisions to the 21st Century Program Coordinator Job description, as amended, 
and forward this item to the full Board of School Committee for approval.  All were in favor and the 
motion passed. 
 
9. Revisions to Policy Students 511: Admission and Tuition of Non-Resident    
Students – by Matt Upton, Esq., Executive Director of Legal and Policy 
 
Executive Director of Legal and Policy Matt Upton presented revisions to Policy Students 511 regarding 
admission and tuition of non-resident students.  Mr. Upton explained that the Board had previously 
amended the policy to allow the District to collect tuition from Education Freedom Account students. 
Recent legislation changed that requirement and now prohibits the District from charging EFA students 
tuition.  The proposed revisions bring the policy into compliance with the new State law.  Mr. Upton 
also explained that Senate Bill 99 affects non-resident students seeking Career and Technical Education 
programming.
August 19, 2026 Policy Committee  
Page 4 of 13 
 
Under the new law, a student attending a private or charter school may access a CTE program if that 
program is geographically closer to the student’s school than the student’s resident CTE program. 
As a result, some non-resident students may attend Manchester School of Technology.  Mr. Upton noted 
that the New Hampshire Department of Education would pay tuition in those circumstances, potentially 
resulting in additional revenue for MST. 
 
There were no questions or comments from the committee. 
 
On motion of Committee Member Taylor, duly seconded by Committee Member O’Neil-Wong, it was 
moved to approve the revisions to policy Students 511: Admission and Tuition of Non-Resident Students, 
and forward this item to the full Board of School Committee for approval.  All were in favor and the 
motion passed. 
 
10. Revisions to Policy Students 562: Participation in Public School Activities – by    
Matt Upton, Esq., Executive Director of Legal and Policy 
 
Mr. Upton presented revisions to Policy Students 562 relating to participation in public school activities. 
He explained that recent legislation requires Education Freedom Account students to be treated similarly 
to private-school and charter-school students for purposes of accessing public-school programs. 
The policy was therefore revised to include EFA students. 
 
Mr. Upton explained that EFA students differ in certain respects from other students.  Enrollment in an 
Education Freedom Account constitutes a parental placement for purposes of special education. 
Therefore, when an EFA student accesses District programming, the District is not required to provide 
the same Free Appropriate Public Education obligation that would apply to a fully enrolled public-
school student.  The revised policy acknowledges that legal distinction. 
 
Mr. Upton also explained that EFA students may not participate in more than 50% of a normal public-
school schedule while remaining enrolled in the EFA program.  If they exceed that threshold, they must 
disenroll from the EFA program.  The Department of Education had recently clarified that the policy 
should state “more than 50%”, rather than “50% or more.”
August 19, 2026 Policy Committee  
Page 5 of 13 
 
Mr. Upton identified several locations within the policy where the language would be corrected and 
stated that an amended version would be provided to the Clerk before the full Board meeting. 
 
Questions and comments from the committee included: 
1. Committee Member Taylor asked how the 50% standard would be calculated.  Mr. Upton stated 
that it would be based upon the normal schedule of a full-time District student rather than the 
student’s outside educational program.  At the high-school level, the Department of Education 
had not yet issued final guidance, although Mr. Upton anticipated that the calculation could be 
based upon credit hours.  At the elementary level, it could potentially be based upon instructional 
time. 
2. Mr. Upton noted that the District had historically seen few students attempting to participate 
part-time while remaining enrolled in the EFA program.  He explained that approximately 50 
students had explored EFA participation during the prior summer but ultimately decided to enroll 
fully in Manchester schools. 
3. The District was working with the Department of Education to establish a method to identify and 
track EFA students.  Mr. Upton stated that the IT Department planned to create an Aspen field 
identifying EFA participants. 
4. Principals and guidance counselors had also been trained so they could monitor enrollment and 
ensure that students did not later add courses that placed them above the allowable threshold. 
5. Mr. Upton expressed concern that the new legislation did not clearly account for extracurricular 
participation, which can also create District costs. 
 
On motion of Committee Member O’Neil-Wong, duly seconded by Committee Member Taylor, it was 
moved to approve the revisions to policy Students 562: Participation in Public School Activities, as 
amended, and forward this item to the full Board of School Committee for approval.  All were in favor 
and the motion passed.
August 19, 2026 Policy Committee  
Page 6 of 13 
 
 
11. Revisions to policy Students 501: Transgender and Non-Conforming Students –    
By Matt Upton, Esq., Executive Director of Legal and Policy 
 
Mr. Upton presented proposed revisions to Policy Students 501 regarding transgender and non-
conforming students.  He explained that the proposed change was related specifically to participation in 
interscholastic and club athletics and was intended to conform District policy with current New 
Hampshire law.  Mr. Upton stated that the policy would require athletic participation to occur in 
accordance with applicable State law and NHIAA rules.  He further explained that the legislation applies 
specifically to interscholastic and club sports. 
 
The policy separately addresses intramural activities.  If an intramural activity is not legally considered a 
club sport, the District could continue allowing transgender students to participate consistent with their 
gender identity. If the activity is considered a club sport, the State law would apply. 
 
Questions and comments from the committee included: 
1. Committee Member St. John asked what would occur if the District left its existing policy 
unchanged.  Mr. Upton stated that the policy would then be inconsistent with State law.  He 
indicated that the District could potentially face a challenge from a parent or another party 
regarding that inconsistency. 
2. Mr. Upton stated that more detailed discussion of potential legal consequences would likely 
constitute legal advice and would therefore be more appropriate in non-public session. 
3. Committee Member St. John stated that he preferred to leave the existing policy unchanged and 
asked whether the Committee could delay action while obtaining additional information.  Mr. 
Upton stated that the Committee could table the item if it wished.  He explained that he was 
attempting to bring forward the package of policy revisions required by recent legislation, but he 
did not believe there was an immediate active case involving a transgender student seeking 
athletic participation in the District. 
4. The Committee discussed whether the item should be tabled at the committee level or forwarded 
to the full Board, where members could remove it from the Consent Agenda and seek legal 
advice before taking final action.
August 19, 2026 Policy Committee  
Page 7 of 13 
 
5. It was noted that tabling the item would keep it at the Policy Committee until its next meeting, 
whereas forwarding the policy would allow the full Board to address the issue sooner. 
 
On motion of Committee Member O’Neil-Wong, duly seconded by Committee Member Potter, it was 
moved to approve the revisions to policy Students 501: Transgender and Non-Conforming Students.  
Committee Members Want and St. John were opposed.  All others were in favor and the motion passed. 
 
The Committee noted that the item could be removed from the Consent Agenda at the full Board 
meeting for additional discussion and legal consultation before final action. 
 
 
12. Parent Group Approval for use of District Name, Logo and Likeness – in     
accordance with policy Community, Agency and Foundations (CAF) 215 – by  
Kelly Jobel, Data/Technology, and Matt Upton, Esq., Executive Director of  
Legal and Policy 
 
Mr. Upton presented requests from two new parent/community organizations seeking recognition and 
permission to use District names, logos, and likenesses in accordance with applicable policy.  The 
organizations were: 
 Little Green Gridiron Club; and 
 Friends of Central Soccer. 
 
There were no questions or comments from the committee. 
 
On motion of Committee Member Taylor, duly seconded by Committee Member O’Neil-Wong, it was 
moved to approve the two additional groups, Little Green Gridiron Club Inc., and Friends of Central 
Soccer, to the Parent Group approval list and forward this item to the full Board of School Committee 
for approval.  All were in favor and the motion passed.
August 19, 2026 Policy Committee  
Page 8 of 13 
 
13. School Safety Facilitator Job Description – by Stacy Champey, Executive     
Director of Safe and Supportive Schools 
 
Stacy Champey, Executive Director of Safe and Supportive Schools, presented revisions to the School 
Safety Facilitator job description.  Ms. Champey explained that the position had been established within 
the previous several years through a grant and in collaboration with the Manchester Police Department. 
The Policy Committee had previously approved a version of the job description during the spring. 
Following feedback from interview candidates, Board members, and the Police Department regarding 
salary and the required skill set, the District revised the position. 
 
The changes included: 
 increasing the number of work days; 
 increasing the salary; 
 expanding responsibilities related to behavioral threat assessment and management; 
 supporting reunification systems; and 
 assisting with certain Title IX investigative responsibilities. 
 
Questions and comments from the committee included: 
1. Committee Member Potter expressed concern that Title IX investigations alone could require 
significant time and that the revised position appeared to require a broad range of specialized 
skills.  The Administration clarified that the School Safety Facilitator would not be the District’s 
sole Title IX investigator. 
2. Dr. Espinola serves as the Title IX Coordinator and may assign investigations to various 
qualified staff. 
3. Ms. Champey stated that her former Assistant Director, who had expertise in behavioral threat 
assessment and management, had resigned from the full-time role but remained available to work 
remotely under contract.  That individual would help provide expertise and support to the School 
Safety Facilitator.  Ms. Champey explained that the former Assistant Director had also 
performed significant work with the Police Department on reunification systems, and the 
Facilitator would help coordinate that work going forward. 
4. The Administration stated that the District was focused on finding the right candidate, given the 
breadth of skills required.
August 19, 2026 Policy Committee  
Page 9 of 13 
 
5. Chair Want clarified that although the position carries a salary, it does not create a general-fund 
fiscal impact because the Manchester Police Department reimburses the District monthly under 
the applicable agreement. 
 
On motion of Committee Member Potter, duly seconded by Committee Member O’Neil-Wong, it was 
moved to approve the revisions to the School Safety Facilitator Job Description and forward this item to 
the full Board of School Committee for approval.  All were in favor and the motion passed. 
 
14. Career Pathway and Work Base Learning Coordinator – by Dr. Kelly Espinola,    
Assistant Superintendent 
 
Dr. Espinola presented revisions to a position at Manchester School of Technology formerly identified 
as a Development Specialist.  The proposed new title is Career Pathway and Work-Based Learning 
Coordinator.  Dr. Espinola explained that MST does not currently have an Extended Learning 
Opportunity Coordinator.  The revised position is intended to align MST more closely with the ELO 
Coordinator positions at the District’s three comprehensive high schools and create a coordinated team 
of four staff members.  The position is funded through the Perkins Grant and does not create a general-
fund fiscal obligation. 
 
Questions and comments from the committee included: 
1. The Committee requested that multilingual preferred be added to the position qualifications. 
2. Committee Member Potter noted that the position summary still contained the previous job title. 
3. Committee Member Potter also questioned why the salary decreased while the number of work 
days increased and responsibilities appeared to remain similar.  Dr. Espinola explained that the 
compensation structure had been aligned with the existing ELO Coordinator positions. 
4. The Administration also clarified that the position was currently vacant and was being revised 
before hiring. 
5. Additional technical corrections were identified, including: 
 correcting the previous title within the position summary; 
 adding spacing between “FERPA” and “confidentiality”; and 
 removing an extra period in the minimum qualifications section.
August 19, 2026 Policy Committee  
Page 10 of 13 
 
On motion of Committee Member Taylor, duly seconded by Committee Member O’Neil-Wong, it was 
moved to approve the revisions to the Career Pathway and Work Base Learning Coordinator Job 
description, as amended,  and forward this item to the full Board of School Committee for approval.  All 
were in favor and the motion passed. 
 
*Superintendent Ryan Roth did not show up for his item on the agenda.  There was discussion on not 
addressing this item; however, due to the time sensitivity of the item, the Committee opted to still review 
this item. 
 
8. 2026/2027 Middle School Handbook – by Ryan Roth, Assistant Superintendent  
 
Dr. Espinola advised the Committee that Mr. Roth was unable to attend the meeting and had sent his 
apologies. She had spoken with him by telephone and had received several updates regarding the proposed 
Middle School Handbook. 
 
The Committee discussed whether to postpone the item because Mr. Roth was not present to answer 
questions. However, because the beginning of the school year was approaching, the Committee agreed to 
proceed with its review.  
 
Dr. Espinola reported that Mr. Roth wanted the Committee to know that all links within the handbook had 
been digitized and were now active electronic links.  She also noted that all four middle schools would 
use the same handbook, creating one unified Middle School Handbook across the District. 
 
Questions and comments from the committee included: 
1. Committee Member St. John noted that the section addressing students’ rights to assembly and 
petition, under the broader free speech and expression provisions, had been crossed out and 
removed from the proposed handbook.  Committee Member St. John requested that the entire 
Assembly and Petition section be restored.  Mr. Upton stated that he was not aware of the reasoning 
behind its proposed removal.  Committee Member St. John indicated that unless there was a 
compelling reason for removing the language, he believed it should remain in the handbook.
August 19, 2026 Policy Committee  
Page 11 of 13 
 
2. The Committee discussed whether the matter should instead be sent to the full Board for discussion 
when Mr. Roth would be available to provide the rationale for the proposed deletion.  Committee 
Member St. John stated that he preferred to restore the language at the committee level. 
3. Committee Member Taylor asked whether comparable language was included in the High School 
Handbook. Administration did not have that information available during the meeting. 
4. Chair Want agreed with Committee Member St. John and stated that the language provided 
students with appropriate rights and responsibilities to have a voice. 
5. The Committee agreed to restore the Assembly and Petition section to the handbook. 
6. Committee Member O’Neil Wong raised several questions regarding the formatting and overall 
presentation of the handbook.  She suggested that the District consider greater consistency in the 
design and formatting of elementary, middle, and high school handbooks.  She noted that 
families may have students attending schools at multiple grade levels and that a consistent format 
would make District handbooks easier to navigate. 
7. Committee Member O’Neil Wong also raised questions regarding tables within the handbook 
that included separate columns for “inappropriate action” and “behavior.” She stated that while 
the distinction might be understood internally, it might not be clear to families reviewing the 
handbook. 
8. Committee Member O’Neil Wong also identified a section involving Level II offenses that 
appeared to be missing a label. 
9. Additional questions were raised regarding the placement of a section concerning reentry plans 
following suspensions and information related specifically to drug and alcohol violations. 
10. Committee members noted that the redlined version of the handbook was difficult to follow 
because the clean version differed significantly in appearance from the version showing 
revisions. 
11. The Committee requested that future revised documents more clearly display both substantive 
changes and formatting changes so members can easily compare the previous and proposed 
versions. 
12. The Committee discussed the amount of material from the Student Code of Conduct that was 
incorporated directly into the Middle School Handbook.  Chair Want noted that some portions of 
the Student Code of Conduct appeared to be reproduced within the handbook while other portions 
were not. She questioned how the District determined which provisions should be repeated in the
August 19, 2026 Policy Committee  
Page 12 of 13 
 
handbook and which should remain solely within the separate Student Code of Conduct.  Dr. 
Espinola explained that Mr. Roth had worked with the middle school principals during the summer 
to ensure consistency among the four schools and determine what should be included. She 
indicated that the material included may represent the issues most commonly encountered at the 
middle school level. 
13. The Committee recognized that the Student Code of Conduct and handbook are separate 
documents and that requiring families to continually move between the two documents could be 
cumbersome. 
14. Members discussed whether including the most commonly applicable provisions directly within 
the handbook may make expectations more accessible to students and families. 
15. Chair Want raised a specific concern regarding the handbook’s language on personal electronic 
devices.  The handbook stated that restrictions on device use apply during the school day and 
specifically referenced lunch periods, homerooms, study halls, recess, passing time, and other 
periods between the first bell and dismissal.  Chair Want noted that bathrooms were not specifically 
included in the list, even though inappropriate cell phone use in bathrooms had repeatedly been 
identified as a concern. Dr. Espinola agreed that students should not be using cell phones in 
bathrooms, particularly because the devices include cameras and video-recording capabilities. 
16. The Committee discussed either specifically adding bathrooms to the list or simply referring 
families back to the District policy.  Chair Want stated that if the handbook was going to provide 
specific examples to make expectations clear to families, bathrooms should also be explicitly 
listed. 
17. It was also noted that the handbook language appeared to have been taken directly from the 
District’s existing personal electronic device policy. The Committee discussed whether that policy 
might also need to be amended in the future to specifically address bathrooms. 
18. Committee Member St. John noted that he had been working on attendance-related matters and 
advised the Committee that, depending on the outcome of that work, the attendance section of the 
handbook might need to be revised in the future. 
19. The Administration confirmed that handbooks are brought back to the Board annually for approval 
and that any necessary attendance revisions could be incorporated into the next handbook cycle. 
20. Mr. Upton agreed with the suggestion that the District examine whether all school handbooks 
could be reformatted to have a similar look, structure, and organization.  He stated that a consistent
August 19, 2026 Policy Committee  
Page 13 of 13 
 
format would make the documents more user-friendly for parents, administrators, faculty, and 
others who may need to reference handbooks across grade levels. Mr. Upton stated that he would 
speak with Assistant Superintendent Nicole Doherty about developing a common format for all 
District handbooks. 
21. The Committee clarified that this would not be completed for the handbook presently under 
consideration. Rather, administration would work on the project throughout the school year and 
potentially into the summer so future handbooks could be presented with a consistent structure. 
22. It was also clarified that questions regarding the “behavior” columns in the revised handbook were 
resolved by reviewing the clean version, where those columns had been removed. 
 
 
On motion of Committee Member St. John, duly seconded by Committee Member Taylor, it was moved 
to approve the 2026/2027 Middle School Handbook, as amended, and forward this item to the full Board 
of School Committee for approval.  All were in favor and the motion passed. 
 
16. TABLED ITEMS  
 
There were no tabled items this evening. 
 
17.   NEW BUSINESS 
 
There was no new business presented. 
 
ADJOURNMENT 
 
18. If there is no further business, a motion is in order to adjourn.  
 
 
On motion of Committee Member Potter , duly seconded by Committee Member O’Neil-Wong , it was 
moved to adjourn.  All were in favor and the meeting adjourned at 6:38 p.m. 
 
True Copy.  Attest. 
Respectfully Submitted, 
  
 
Clerk of Committee
